reasoning: Upper bound: In any 8 consecutive integers {a,...,a+7}, the pairs differing by 3 or 5 form a single 8-cycle (a, a+3, a+6, a+1, a+4, a+7, a+2, a+5, back to a), so at most 4 of them can be chosen. Partition {1..50} = {1} ∪ {2..9} ∪ {10..17} ∪ ... ∪ {42..49} ∪ {50}: this gives at most 1+6·4+1 = 26, with equality only if 1 and 50 are both chosen and each block contributes 4. If 1 is chosen, 4 and 6 are excluded; in the 8-cycle on {2..9} (7-2-5-8-3-6-9-4-7) deleting 4 and 6 leaves the path 7-2-5-8-3 plus isolated 9, and the only independent 4-set is {3,5,7,9}. Then 9 excludes 12,14 and the same argument forces {11,13,15,17} from {10..17}, and inductively {43,45,47,49} from {42..49}. But 50 differs from 47 by 3 (and from 45 by 5), contradiction. Hence 26 is impossible and the maximum is at most 25. Construction: the 25 odd numbers {1,3,5,...,49}; any two differ by an even number, so never by 3 or 5. Therefore the maximum is 25.
